assigned.title: Settings a viewer can actually change
assigned.acceptance: There is a settings screen, and every switch on it changes something real. Neither a screen nor an API exists today. REQUIRED: preferred audio and subtitle languages, persisted per profile and consumed as PW-0206's defaults rather than as a second policy. REQUIRED: a diagnostics and telemetry control that is honest about what it does -- telemetry-decision.ts already reports WHY telemetry is off, and that reasoning belongs in front of the viewer instead of in a details element in the player. REQUIRED: an about section naming the application version and the licences the installer must carry, which is where PW-0208's LGPL attribution obligation is discharged in the product. REQUIRED: no setting weakens a security or rights control; there is no 'allow insecure sources' switch and no way to disable the transport checks.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck: 22 tasks successful, 0 failures. Separately npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json alone (exit 0, no output) and npx tsc --noEmit -p e2e/tsconfig.json (exit 0) -- the e2e harness is outside the workspaces and its own typecheck is a separate CI job, so a spec that compiles only under the root project would still be red there. One defect was caught by that second command and fixed rather than worked around: the spec read apps/web/package.json through import.meta.url, and e2e/tsconfig.json emits CommonJS, where the meta-property is unavailable; it now resolves through __dirname, with the reason recorded at the line.

unit.evidence:
npx vitest run apps/web: 95 files, 1714 tests, 0 failures. The whole repository under npx vitest run apps/web packages/contracts packages/persistence: 119 files, 2262 passed, 1 skipped.

WHAT THIS TASK ADDED OR CHANGED, AND WHAT EACH ONE IS FOR:

apps/web/src/components/settings/settings.test.tsx -- 13 cases, new. The language field's PARSE is pinned over the five inputs that matter: order preserved ("ja, en, de"), whitespace and empties dropped but never a tag, an empty field answering [] rather than [""] (which would reach the endpoint and be refused for something the viewer did not type), a lossless round trip with formatLanguageList, and case left alone because the ENDPOINT owns what a language tag is and a client that lower-cased first would be a second validator whose message a viewer never sees. Two source rules on the form: it mentions no profileId anywhere (the endpoint derives the profile from the session and its contract is .strict(), so the component could not address another household's settings even by accident), and it applies state from the RESPONSE on both paths rather than from the inputs. The diagnostics section is asserted by COMPUTING decidePlaybackTelemetry independently with the same inputs and requiring the rendered page to agree, code by code -- so a change to the decision that this screen stopped reflecting fails here instead of misleading a viewer -- plus a source rule that it offers no control at all, because a toggle wired to nothing is the fake persistence the round-110 instruction forbids by name. About is asserted twice deliberately: the rendered version equals package.json's, AND the source contains no version-shaped literal, because the first assertion passes either way and only the second catches a paste.

apps/web/src/app/watch/watch-session.test.ts -- 5 cases added, 30 total, all passing. These are where the acceptance's "consumed as PW-0206's defaults" is actually proven, and they pin the three states apart: null (nobody has chosen) sends CONSERVATIVE_CAPABILITIES unchanged; a list sends it with preferredAudioLanguages replaced, IN THE VIEWER'S ORDER (asserted as a sequence, not a set -- the contract says order is meaningful); and [] sends the empty list, which is the case that forces the caller to carry `stored` rather than collapsing an opt-out into a default. A fourth pins the BLAST RADIUS -- the key set is identical to the baseline and every key except preferredAudioLanguages is unchanged, written that way so a capability field added later is covered without anybody remembering -- because every other field is a claim about what the DEVICE can decode and a settings screen must not be able to widen one. A fifth proves the list is copied, so a later mutation of the repository's array cannot change a request already described.

apps/web/src/lib/viewer-preferences.test.ts -- 3 cases, new, and the header states plainly what this environment can and cannot see. The loader resolves the REAL repository adapter and the REAL identity system, exactly as loadResumePosition does, so no store is injected and no success path is faked here. What is pinned is the property that holds in every configuration and is the one a playback page depends on: a read that cannot be satisfied answers stored:false with the neutral value rather than throwing, the direction matters (stored:true with empty lists would be an opt-out the viewer never expressed), and the shared constant it returns is frozen so one caller cannot mutate what the next render sees.

A CORRECTION MADE WHILE WRITING THIS, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS A REAL MISTAKE. The first draft of loadMediaPreferences returned MediaPreferences alone, with a comment arguing the stored/not-stored distinction "does not matter to the media engine". That was wrong, and the first caller proved it: an unconfigured profile must keep getting ["en"] and a cleared profile must get [], and both have empty lists. The loader now returns StoredMediaPreferences and the wrong comment is replaced by the reasoning at the same place rather than quietly deleted.

e2e.evidence:
TWO CONFIGURATIONS, BOTH FULL SUITES, BOTH CHROMIUM (the only browser ci.yml installs).

PRODUCTION BUILD + REAL POSTGRESQL (LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/lib_wl, port 3177, --workers=1): 88 cases, 49 passed, 39 skipped, 0 failed, 1.1m.
DEVELOPMENT BUILD (LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development): 88 cases, 67 passed, 21 skipped, 0 failed, 2.4m.

e2e/tests/settings.spec.ts ALONE against production + PostgreSQL: 9 passed, 0 failed, 1.1m. All nine, named:

GROUP A, true in every configuration -- the About section names the version apps/web/package.json declares (READ FROM THE REAL FILE at run time, not written into the spec, so it cannot rot at the next release); it names THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md AND carries the sentence that it does not inspect your installation, because PW-0208 is the task that proves a packaged tree really carries it and a screen that claimed otherwise would make the attribution problem worse; the diagnostics section shows the collector path and at least one real reason code; and the screen offers no switch that could weaken a security or rights control -- asserted as an absence of the VOCABULARY ("allow insecure", "disable transport", "skip verification", "ignore certificate", "developer mode", "unsafe") rather than of a particular control id, because that defect would arrive under a name nobody has chosen yet, with a non-vacuity check that the page under those assertions is the real one.

GROUP B, against a real signed-in session and real rows -- "a choice survives a reload, WHICH IS WHAT TELLS PERSISTENCE FROM STATE": the profile is put back to not-chosen through the API first so the starting state is made true rather than inherited, then ja/en is typed, saved, AND THE PAGE RELOADED, and the values are still there. Everything before the reload would pass against a component that remembered the typing and never spoke to a server, which is exactly what the round-110 instruction forbade. "the order is kept" saves a deliberately non-alphabetical pt-BR, ja, en and reads back the sequence, because a store that round-tripped the membership would satisfy a careless test and hand the media engine a different answer. "clearing is not the same as leaving the lists empty" saves two EMPTY lists, reloads and gets "these are your choices", then clears, reloads and gets "you have not chosen yet" -- same empty fields, opposite meanings, which is what makes the API's `stored` flag load-bearing rather than decorative. "a language tag the contract refuses is reported, not silently dropped" types "english", requires the alert AND the absence of the success sentence, then RELOADS to prove nothing was stored -- the alert alone could be shown by a client that wrote anyway. "a viewer who is not signed in is offered the way in" sets no session headers at all, so it is the real signed-out branch, and asserts the languages form is absent while About and Diagnostics are still present, because hiding an attribution obligation behind a sign-in withholds it from the person least able to go looking for it.

A PRECONDITION THAT HAD TO BE FIXED FIRST, AND IS NOT PAPERED OVER HERE. The local database did not have profile_media_preference, because .github/workflows/ci.yml applied migration 0000 BY NAME and PL-0723 added 0001. It was applied by hand to run the above, and the underlying defect is PL-0726, which is fixed, gated against a real PostgreSQL and in review in this same bundle. WITHOUT PL-0726 THIS GATE WOULD BE LOCAL-ONLY AND CI WOULD BE RED -- group B does not skip, since LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL is set and DATABASE_SESSION_SKIP_REASON is therefore null. Stated rather than left for CI to discover.

WHAT THIS SPEC DOES NOT CLAIM, written into its header: it does not assert that a stored language changes which audio track PLAYS. The e2e catalog is fixtures and nothing here has a multi-audio title, so an audible claim would be an inference. What the preference actually reaches is the playback SESSION REQUEST, and that is proven directly in watch-session.test.ts over all three states with the body parsed by the route's own strict schema.

ENVIRONMENT NOTE, NOT A CHANGE TO ANYTHING PINNED: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH had to be pointed at ~/.cache/ms-playwright, because this container's /opt/pw-browsers holds revision 1194 while the pinned @playwright/test 1.62.1 wants 1234. firefox, webkit and mobile-safari are UNVERIFIED here -- their binaries are absent from the container -- and are not run in CI either, which installs chromium and nothing else.

assigned.title: Corrective: the roving group sets state inside an effect, and repository lint is red
assigned.acceptance:
`npm run lint` FAILS AT THE REPOSITORY LEVEL on a file PW-0310 shipped in round 109:

  apps/web/src/lib/a11y/roving-group.tsx:198:5
  error  Calling setState synchronously within an effect can trigger cascading renders  react-hooks/set-state-in-effect

Confirmed to pre-exist this round's work: stashing the working-tree change and re-running eslint against the COMMITTED file reproduces the same error at the same line. PW-0310's declared gates are typecheck, unit, e2e and architecture-review -- there is no lint gate on it -- so no gate was falsified; the check that would have caught this was not among the ones the task had to run.

THERE ARE TWO setState CALLS IN THAT EFFECT AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT PROBLEMS. `setMounted(true)` is a hydration guard: the first client render must reproduce the server's markup, so the arrow-key instruction in `aria-description` may only appear once the keys actually work. `setActive(settled)` writes a CLAMPED index back into state when a shrinking rail has left the stored index past the end.

REQUIRED: the lint error is gone and `npm run lint` is green at the repository level.
REQUIRED: the hydration guard still holds -- the server render must still carry no `aria-description`, and the client must still gain one. Announcing 'use the arrow keys' on a page where nothing is listening for them is a false promise to a screen-reader user, and deleting the guard to satisfy a lint rule would make that promise.
REQUIRED: a stale active index still cannot send focus to a card that is not there. If the write-back is removed, the clamp must move to every point of use -- note that `nextActive` is NOT safe against an out-of-range `current`: ArrowLeft from index 7 in a 3-card rail returns 6.
REQUIRED: the keyboard e2e gate (`e2e/tests/keyboard-reachability.spec.ts`, including its two planted-failure cases) still passes against a real browser. A refactor of focus management that is only unit-tested is not evidenced.

FORBIDDEN: an eslint-disable comment, a rule downgrade or removal in the eslint config, or any change that makes the command green without changing the behaviour the rule is objecting to. The rule is right: a synchronous setState in an effect is an extra render pass on every mount, and the rule cannot tell this one from a cascade.
NOT IN SCOPE: the two pre-existing lint WARNINGS elsewhere in apps/web (`_omitted` and `WatchlistEntryRow` unused). They are warnings, they are not this file, and bundling them here would widen a corrective task into a cleanup.
assigned.notes: FILED ROUND 110 by claude-lead after `npm run lint` failed during PW-0308's gate sequence. Filed rather than fixed inside PW-0308 because apps/web/src/lib/a11y/** is PW-0310's surface and PW-0310 is DONE: reaching into a closed task's files from an in-progress one would be the silent surface broadening the standing constraints forbid.

unit.evidence: npx vitest run apps/web -- 95 files, 1714 tests, 0 failures. Includes the new apps/web/src/lib/a11y/roving-group.test.tsx (7 tests), which asserts the half neither existing suite could see: the SERVER render carries no aria-description, no arrow-key instruction and no tabindex, for both the ul and div shapes. Its three source rules carry non-vacuity checks -- the effect-body rule asserts the effect was actually found before asserting what is absent from it, so a refactor that renamed the effect fails loudly rather than passing emptily. roving.test.ts (17 tests) and keyboard-reachability.test.ts (25 tests) unchanged and passing.

e2e.evidence: npx playwright test tests/keyboard-reachability.spec.ts --project=chromium --workers=1 against a real next dev server on port 3177 (LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development): 10 passed, 0 failed, 42.4s. The ten include the two PLANTED-FAILURE cases -- 'THE GATE ITSELF FAILS WHEN SOMETHING IS UNREACHABLE' and 'THE ROVING-GROUP CHECK ITSELF FAILS WHEN A RAIL LOSES ITS ENTRY POINT' -- so the suite is proven non-vacuous in the same run, and 'ARROW KEYS MOVE ALONG A RAIL, and Tab then leaves it', which is the behaviour this change refactored. CHROMIUM ONLY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE GATE SURFACE, NOT A NARROWING: ci.yml's e2e job runs 'npx playwright install chromium' and nothing else. The firefox, webkit and mobile-safari projects are UNVERIFIED here -- their browser binaries are absent from this container (browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at /root/.cache/ms-playwright/firefox-1538/firefox/firefox) and they are not run in CI either.
